title: Multisensory Gamma Entrainment
description: EEG dataset from a single healthy young adult examining how auditory, visual, and combined audio-visual stimulation entrain gamma-band brain oscillations. Gamma entrainment has been proposed as a therapeutic approach for Alzheimer's disease symptoms. The session consists of three 40-second stimulation epochs, using a 40 Hz amplitude-modulated auditory tone, a 20 Hz LED flicker, and both together.
methods_description: EEG was recorded from 19 monopolar channels in the 10/20 system, referenced to the earlobes, at a 500 Hz sampling rate, with impedance kept under 20 kOhm. The auditory stimulus was a 5 kHz carrier tone modulated by a 40 Hz rectangular wave with a 4% duty cycle. The visual stimulus was a 20 Hz white LED flicker with a 50% duty cycle. Preprocessing used EEGLAB and included 1 Hz high-pass filtering, line noise removal, bad channel rejection and interpolation, average re-referencing, Artifact Subspace Reconstruction, ICA, and dipole fitting.
